conventions.scope: Independent source-blind public-behavior workload. No case has been executed. Execution must wait for independent semantic/action-binding review and complete freeze.
conventions.distribution: Exactly 12 cases: four English, four Español, four English + Español.
fixture: Use a plain-text host. Prepare each initial host text and caret through ordinary host editing before the numbered actions. Each case starts independently.
Host transformations, keyboard auto-capitalization, autocorrection, smart punctuation, and learning are OFF for all exact literal comparisons.
Use the stated language mode. Start on letter keys unless stated otherwise. Establish initial settings before numbered actions.
Caret notation uses | for the insertion point; | is never literal host text. Existing emoji history is unspecified unless a case creates a known entry.
action_binding: Each case contains at most six numbered public actions. A finite listed sequence of key taps is performed in order. A settings visit means opening public settings, changing only the named controls, observing their displayed values, and returning to the keyboard.
Check each outcome immediately after its referenced action. Observe host text and caret through the ordinary host UI; do not use private APIs, logs, or internal state.

For cursor editing, hold the space bar and slide in the named direction until the visibly indicated host caret reaches the stated character boundary, then release. No fixed distance or duration is required.

For slide typing, trace the named visible letter keys in one continuous gesture and release. Require a committed nonempty text span, without an exact glide word, spelling, ranking, prediction, or boundary-spacing oracle. Capture actual resulting host text and caret when requested.

Before every emoji selection, record the full actually displayed selectable emoji as the named variable, including any variation selectors, modifiers, or joined components. Tap that same displayed result. Never assume a fixed identity or ranking.

Open/focus emoji search through its public UI and type its queries using keyboard letter keys. Search Backspace refers to the key while the keyboard-local search field has focus. Until a result is selected, query typing and editing must preserve host text and caret.
An ordinary query requiring a visible selectable result checks search availability only. No particular emoji identity, order, or count is required.
Recent-choice checks assert visible membership of the recorded emoji, with no exact ordering, count, uniqueness, or assumption of empty history.

Physical sound and tactile haptics are unavailable observations on Simulator. Record both as unavailable on Simulator; neither is an impossible release prerequisite. Feedback cases assert independent displayed settings and editing continuity.
conventions.variables: All variables are case-local observations recorded before their dependent actions. Concatenation means exact text joining with no added characters unless explicitly stated.
conventions.exclusions: No performance thresholds, population claims, inaccessible internals, dictionary-quality oracle, or persistence across reinstall/reboot.

Tap the space bar once, then letter keys o, n in order.

Host is exactly redsu on blue; caret is redsu on| blue. Existing suffix remains intact.

actions: Open the emoji picker and focus its keyboard-local search field.
Tap letter keys c, a, t to enter cat.
Tap search Backspace once, then letter key r to change the query to car.
Record one visible selectable result full emoji as E, then tap that same result.
Return to letter keys and tap letter key z.
Open the emoji picker and show recent choices.

Query is exactly cat; host remains note with unchanged caret.
Query is exactly car and at least one selectable result is visible. Host remains note with unchanged caret; search deletion does not delete host text.

Host is exactly the concatenation of note, E, and z; caret is at end.
Recent choices visibly contain E. Opening recents preserves host text and caret.

cases.rationale: Checks query isolation and correction, observed-result selection, letter-entry continuity, and recent-choice history.

actions: Slide continuously over c, a, t and release; record resulting host text as G.
In settings turn Show Slide Trail OFF, leave Slide to Type ON, and return to the keyboard.
Tap letter key q.
Slide continuously over d, o, g and release; record resulting host text as H.
In settings turn Slide to Type OFF, leave Show Slide Trail OFF, and return to the keyboard.
Tap letter key v.

expected_outcomes.checkpoint: A visible trail follows the gesture and a nonempty text span is committed. Record actual G; caret follows the committed text. No exact word is required.
Slide to Type is ON and Show Slide Trail is OFF. Both feedback settings remain OFF. Host and caret are unchanged.
Host is exactly G concatenated with q; caret is at end.
No slide trail is displayed during the gesture; a nonempty slide-typed span is committed at the caret. Record actual resulting H without an exact spelling or boundary-spacing requirement.
Slide to Type and Show Slide Trail are OFF. Both feedback settings remain OFF. Host and caret are unchanged.
Host is exactly H concatenated with v; caret is at end. Tap typing works with Slide to Type OFF.

cases.rationale: Separates trail visibility from slide input, checks application on return, and checks tap continuity after disabling slide input.
